<explanation>
Based on the provided file tree and README, I'll explain how to create a comprehensive system design diagram for this Onetime Secret application. This is a full-stack web application focused on secure, one-time message sharing.

1. Main Components to Include:

a) Frontend Layer:
- Vue.js application (src/ directory)
- Components structure (/src/components)
- State management with Pinia (/src/stores)
- Routing system (/src/router)
- Internationalization support (/src/locales)

b) Backend Layer:
- Ruby application (lib/ directory)
- API versions (v1 and v2)
- Web interface handlers
- Authentication system
- Email handling system

c) Data Storage:
- Redis database
- Secret storage
- Session management
- Rate limiting

d) External Services:
- SMTP/SendGrid for email delivery
- Stripe integration for payments
- Domain verification system

2. Component Relationships:

Draw the diagram with these connections:
```
[Client Browser] ←→ [Frontend (Vue.js)]
                    ↓
[Load Balancer/Reverse Proxy]
                    ↓
[Backend (Ruby/Thin Server)]
    ↓           ↓           ↓
[Redis DB] [Email Service] [Stripe]
```

3. Color Coding:

- Blue: Frontend components
- Green: Backend services
- Red: Data storage
- Yellow: External services
- Purple: Security/Authentication layers

4. Detailed Component Breakdown:

Frontend (Vue.js):
```
[Vue Router] → [Vue Components] → [Pinia Stores]
     ↓              ↓               ↓
[API Client] ← [Authentication] → [State Management]
```

Backend (Ruby):
```
[Thin Server]
     ↓
[Rack Middleware]
     ↓
[App Routes (Web/API)]
     ↓
[Logic Layer]
     ↓
[Models Layer]
     ↓
[Redis Adapter]
```

- CSRF protection

6. Key Integration Points:

- API endpoints (/lib/onetime/app/api/v1 and v2)

- Frontend-backend communication
- Redis connection points
- External service integrations

7. Deployment Architecture:

- Docker container structure
- Redis instance
